coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Potrero Power Station Block 7 (remaining portion)
record.summary: The L-shaped southwestern portion of Block 7 at Humboldt St and Louisiana Paseo, approved March 2, 2022 for a Foster + Partners-designed 27-story, approximately 237-ft market-rate tower with 325 units, ground-floor retail and childcare over a basement garage; the tallest building permitted on the site. No building permit or construction start has been reported as of September 2026.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built and does not correspond to any subdivided Assessor parcel: it currently sits on vacant/graded land within the former power station site (unaddressed in DataSF's Assessor roll). Traced from an adopted regulatory diagram, fitted to real street positions at multiple points, but this diagram is dated 2020 and may not reflect later design changes (as already found for the UCSF/Sophie Maxwell area). Treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 10-25m, not survey-grade, and treat the block's applicability itself as somewhat more provisional than Mission Rock's or Pier 70's equivalent entries. The shape was rebuilt on 2026-09-16 with a more careful fit of the diagram to the map, re-measured the same day consistently across the whole block layout, and corrected again that day after one mis-measured reference point was fixed. How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its data file in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record). CLIPPED 2026-09-17: although this record's regulatory notes already said the shape was 'clipped to exclude Sophie Maxwell's real footprint,' a fresh check of overlaps between real parcels and approximate shapes found this polygon still overlapped Sophie Maxwell (block/lot 4232020) by 1,082 sq m -- the clip described in that text was apparently never actually applied to (or was lost from) the published shape. It was then re-clipped against block/lot 4232020's real parcel boundary; area dropped from ~4,965 to ~3,883 sq m. This overlap had gone undetected because Pier & Point's automated shape check only compared approximate shapes with each other, never with real parcels. The vacant/graded and unaddressed-in-the-Assessor-roll wording is our own observation, not something the cited 2020 D4D can show; 'not yet built' is consistent with the 2024 annual compliance report (March 2025), which says the developer had submitted no building permits for any market-rate housing projects. The 2020 date of the diagram is confirmed by the final D4D's footer (February 26, 2020). DataSF Parcels (queried 2026-09-29) lists active lots in Assessor blocks 4175 and 4232 added in December 2023 after the Phase 1 Final Map, most unaddressed; whether one of them corresponds to this block was not checked, so the statement that no subdivided Assessor parcel exists for it is unverified.
notes.digitized_from: Potrero Power Station Design for Development, Figure 6.2.3 - Building Height Plan (p.245).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor parcel may exist under this block (part of the site's larger, largely unaddressed footprint), but it has not been subdivided per the masterplan's individual named blocks -- this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead. (This is Pier & Point's own parcel search, not something the cited Design for Development can establish; the D4D does not address Assessor parcels.) DataSF Parcels (queried 2026-09-29) shows at least 22 active lots in Assessor blocks 4175 and 4232 added in December 2023 following the Phase 1 Final Map recorded July 26, 2022 (most unaddressed; e.g. 4232022 = 151 Humboldt St, 4232020 = 1212 Maryland St); whether one of them matches this block was not checked.
notes.regulatory_context: Figure 6.2.3 of the final D4D (printed p.245) shows Block 7 as one numbered block, with its height zones read from the figure's colour-coded labels: the north-west part (on Humboldt St at Louisiana Paseo) is labelled 240'/85' (maximum height 240 ft, maximum base height 85 ft) and the rest of the block (east side and south strip) is 85'; the two '150'MAX' markings are plan dimensions of the tower, not heights. The D4D numbers only 'Block 7'; 'Block 7A' and 'Block 7B' are the names SF Planning's own approvals use for the two buildings (e.g. 'Approval of the Design Review Application of Block 7A', March 2, 2022, Case 2017-011878PHA-04, and Block 7B, March 2, 2022). The Sophie Maxwell Building ('Block 7b, the Sophie Maxwell Building' in the 2024 annual compliance report; real blklot 4232020, addressed 1212 MARYLAND in DataSF Parcels; already mapped separately in this dataset) occupies part of this block; this polygon is the REMAINING portion, clipped to exclude Sophie Maxwell's real footprint (the clipping is our own work). The remainder is presumed to correspond to 'Block 7A' (Foster + Partners-designed rental tower, press-reported heights of 240-264 ft depending on source, consistent with this figure's 240 ft max) -- design review approved March 2, 2022; the 2024 annual compliance report says no market-rate building permits had been submitted; no construction-start source found.

changes.text: Block 7's heights now follow the Design for Development's colour-coded labels: a 240 ft maximum with an 85 ft base in the north-west part and 85 ft elsewhere (the earlier '150 ft base' was a plan dimension). The unit list no longer includes 315, which is Block 8's figure on the Planning Commission slides, and the 27-story and 325-unit figures are attributed to SF YIMBY rather than the slides. The design review application date now follows Planning's memo (December 19, 2020). The expected completion moved from 2028 (a press figure) to 2029, the end of Phase 1's schedule in the October 2020 approval, and is marked soft because earlier 2020 forecasts did not hold. 'Market-rate rental' now says the developer anticipates rental units. The Foster + Partners rendering was removed because the plan sheets are marked as copyrighted by the architect; the design review packet remains cited. The dead 2019 draft link was replaced with the final February 2020 document and the Fifth Space rename no longer carries a year.

open_questions: Construction start: none found. Searched the 2021-2024 DA compliance reports (the 2024 report says no market-rate building permits have been submitted), SF YIMBY through Sept 2026, the Chronicle (Jul 29 and Aug 3, 2026), SF Standard (Oct 2025) and Potrero View (Oct 2025). SocketSite (Jul 2021) said construction was 'slated to commence in 2023'; SF YIMBY (Mar 2021) said Block 7 construction was expected to start 'by 2023, with completion by 2026'. Neither happened.

Whether the July 2026 Chronicle line 'tallest residential tower would be permitted to reach 248 feet' refers to Block 7A: the D4D allows 240-ft highrise towers on both Block 5 and Block 7, and the amendment package also lets Block 5 flip between residential and commercial. Not confirmed for 7A specifically; the Planning Commission packet for July 30, 2026 was not reviewed.

Unit count drift: 277 (press 2021) -> 325 (approval 2022) -> 319 (compliance reports' LBE appendix); the Planning Commission slides (July 2021) show '315' only on the 'Previous Phase 1' map inside Block 8 and '420' for Block 7 (7A with 7b) on the 'Current Phase 1' slide, so no slide gives a 7A-only count. Which figure a future permit will carry is unknown.

SF Standard (Oct 15, 2025) says Associate Capital 'will move on to constructing a 300-unit market-rate apartment building' next; the Aug 2026 Chronicle names Block 8 (342 units) as the next building, so 7A does not appear to be next.

Ground-floor childcare (6,000 GSF per DA Phasing Plan) is assigned to Block 7 in the compliance reports; the April 2023 childcare/HPP phasing amendment was not read for this record and may have moved it.
No cost, financing, general contractor or ground-lease information exists for Block 7A in any source found; the land is developer-owned (not Port), so no Port lease applies.

The 'Block 7A' / 'Block 7B' names are the sponsor's; the D4D treats Block 7 as one block with a single 240-ft highrise envelope. This record's map-shape note saying 7A/7B are 'informal press/developer labels' is consistent with the Planning documents, which nonetheless use 7A/7B as case names.

Block 7A rendering (Foster + Partners indicative views from the Design Review Approval packet) removed from the images shown here on 2026-09-29: the plan sheets are marked '(c) Foster + Partners 2020', which is not a licence to host them. The packet remains cited as a source (the Block 7A Design Review Approval); linked, not hosted.
